references.text: Jacob's vow begins in this verse with the conditions: If God will be with him, keep him on his way, give him food and clothing. Verse 21 is the direct continuation of this vow.
The Lord tells Jacob to return to the land of his fathers and to his relatives, and that He will be with him. This reflects Jacob's vow to return to his father's house in peace.
Jacob arrived safely (shalem) at the city of Shechem in the land of Canaan when he came from Paddan-Aram. This is the fulfillment of Jacob's vow to return in peace (beshalom).

Jacob says they should go up to Bethel, where he will build an altar to God who answered him on the day of his flight and who has been with him on the way he went. This shows the fulfillment of Jacob's vow that the Lord will be his God.
Israel declares that the Lord shall be their God, and they will walk in His ways. The covenant language 'The Lord shall be my God' in Gen 28:21 is an early expression of this covenant formula.
Jacob's conditional vow to acknowledge the Lord as his God (Gen 28:21) is fulfilled and confirmed in Israel's national confession after the exodus from Egypt (Ex 15:2).
Jacob's personal vow that the Lord shall be his God (Gen 28:21) is a microcosmic precursor to the great prophetic promise of God's eternal dwelling and covenant with the people in Ezekiel's time.
